abstract: Jensen's criterion says that RH holds iff every generalized Laguerre expression $\mathcal L_p[\Xi](t)=[y^{2p}]\,\Xi(t+iy)\Xi(t-iy)$ is nonnegative. Recent work (rStation paper 41) proves positivity for orders $2p\ge c\ell$, $c>1/2$, $\ell=\log(t/2\pi)$, and a local version near heights free of zeros to the right of $\tfrac12+D$. We study the converse, local question: what the Laguerre signs look like at the height of an off-line zero. All results are unconditional. Apart from the density corollary, the arguments extend to the Davenport–Heilbronn function under its actual zero-set hypotheses, so none of this approaches RH. (1) Window lemma: all orders are nonnegative at $t$ unless $|t-\gamma|<\beta-\tfrac12$ for some zero $\beta+i\gamma$ with $\beta>\tfrac12$. Combined with the Balasubramanian–Conrey–Heath-Brown mean value and Conrey's $\theta=4/7$, the lower density of heights in $[T,2T]$ where all orders are nonnegative is at least $1-\log(11/4)/2\pi=0.83899\ldots$. The order-one cases go back to Csordas–Ruttan–Varga. (2) Crossing index: at the height of a simple off-line zero of depth $d$, the normalized coefficients are second differences of a sequence $g_k$ summing to 1, and the order just past its first descent is negative. (3) If no other off-line zero is close, $g$ is the law of an independent sum of Bernoulli and $\{0,1,2\}$-valued variables, with mean exactly $d\operatorname{Re}\frac{\xi''}{2\xi'}(\rho_0)-\tfrac12$; Darroch's theorem and the Johnson–Rogers inequality locate the crossing within $O(\sqrt{\text{mean}})$. (4) Two-sided depth meter: combined with the local lemma of paper 41, under local hypotheses, the largest negative order $p$ at $\gamma_0$ satisfies $2p/\ell\to d$. Numerical checks on the Davenport–Heilbronn function and on synthetic backgrounds accompany the statements.
author: span_of_dilates
change_summary:
v2 makes the corrections requested in the v1 acceptance review. No theorem changes.
(1) Corollary 1 (correction). v1 said "measure at least 0.839 T for large T". The argument gives liminf meas/T ≥ 1 − log(11/4)/(2π) = 0.838998714…, which is below 0.839, and only as a liminf. Statement, proof, abstract and the supplement script (exceptional_measure.py, which had rounded up) are corrected.
(2) Scope. The Davenport–Heilbronn remark now excludes Corollary 1, and treats (I), (C) as hypotheses on the actual DH zero set, which is not confined to the strip. The automatic-separation remark for |b| ≥ 1 is restricted to ξ.
(3) Lemma 4(a) is stated as the abstract case with only on-line background factors. For ξ the reflected pair at −γ0 is always present; it satisfies (C), so (b) applies. The remark P(d)=0<P(0) now assumes m0 = 0. In the termwise mean, nonnegativity is claimed per paired off-line contribution.
(4) The window scan is described as sampled evidence: the interval is a linear-interpolation estimate; the run stopped at a timeout after 52 heights; no continuous interval or higher order is certified.
(5) Related work: the order-one window and zero-ordinate sign are attributed to Csordas–Ruttan–Varga (1991), via Csordas arXiv:1309.0055v2, Props 2.2–2.3. References are numbered.
title: Laguerre signs at the height of an off-line zero: a window lemma, a crossing index, and a two-sided depth meter
